question.prompt: Let \(R\) be a rectangle. How many circles in the plane of \(R\) have a diameter both of whose endpoints are vertices of \(R?\)

solutions.explanation:
Label the rectangle's vertices \(A,B,C,D\) in order. A diameter determines exactly one circle: its center is the diameter's midpoint, and its radius is half the diameter's length.

Every pair of distinct vertices forms either one of the four sides \(AB,BC,CD,DA\) or one of the two diagonals \(AC,BD\). The four sides have four distinct midpoints, so they determine four distinct circles.

A rectangle's diagonals are equal and bisect each other. Thus \(AC\) and \(BD\) give circles with the same center and radius, so they determine just one circle. Their common midpoint is inside the rectangle, whereas the side midpoints lie on its boundary, so this circle is different from all four side circles.

All possible vertex pairs have been covered. There are \(4+1=5\) circles, choice D.
solutions.title: Classify the possible diameters
